v0.2.change: The log-income sd passed to the provider is multiplied by sqrt(1 - rho^2) before discretisation, so the chain has unconditional sd sd*sqrt(1 - rho^2) instead of sd.
v0.2.plausible: Aiyagari (1994) writes the innovation as sigma*(1 - rho^2)^(1/2), and a programmer who believes the Rouwenhorst routine takes the innovation sd passes that product instead of the unconditional sd.
v0.2.why: The chain gets unconditional sd sd*sqrt(1-rho^2) (0.44 sd at rho = 0.9). The no-risk limit, its O(eps^2) rate and the monotonicity in sd hold for any rescaling of risk. Monotonicity in rho at sd = 0.4 now compares effective sd 0.40, 0.38, 0.32, 0.17 for rho = 0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9, so persistence and risk size move r in opposite directions (T4 unsure). Steady-state identities, E[e] = 1 and the pins hold; the income-process sd is not pinned (V miss).

patches.old: e, pi, Pi = rouwenhorst(rho, sd, p['n_e'])
patches.new: e, pi, Pi = rouwenhorst(rho, sd * np.sqrt(1 - rho ** 2), p['n_e'])

v0.2.change: The exogenous step of the Young-lottery chain uses kron(Pi, I) instead of kron(Pi', I), so mass moves with the rows of Pi and the stationary income marginal becomes uniform instead of the Markov chain's stationary distribution.
v0.2.plausible: Row- versus column-stochastic conventions are easy to mix up when building a sparse forward operator by hand, and kron(Pi, I) still yields a normalisable distribution without any error.
v0.2.reach: T1 T2 T3 T4 T5 T6 D
v0.2.why: FastHetBlock's chain moves mass with Pi instead of Pi': its stationary Dbeg has a uniform income marginal, and SSJ's D = Pi' Dbeg is not stationary under SSJ's own law of motion. D compares with SSJ's forward iteration (catch). End-of-period and next beginning-of-period mean assets differ, so households earn interest on a different stock than the government pays on: T5 Walras under rate shocks (as M13). T4: brentq still clears the market on the mis-aggregated A, and the Euler errors use the policy (miss). V2: household budget C - r A - sum(pi y) != 0.

v0.2.change: The central finite difference of the cohort consumption paths is divided by h instead of 2h, doubling every cohort iMPC path.

v0.2.why: Cohort paths doubled: sum_k mu_k dC_k = 2 M x (test_wealth_group_split_adds_up). No V test reads t6.

v0.2.plausible: Since r_t is the ex-post return on assets bought at t-1, a programmer can reason that the rate was set at t-1 and so should respond to date t-1 output.
v0.2.why: A different but internally consistent rule: IKC and Walras hold on the solver's paths, the fixed-rate shocks and T6 (fixed r) are untouched. The F2 pin may turn XPASS because the rule-based system changes (T5 unsure). V4(b) checks the documented contemporaneous rule on the path: residual phi_y (dY_{t-1} - dY_t).

v0.2.change: The countercyclical incidence is normalised so that sum_i pi_i zeta_i = 0 instead of sum_i pi_i e_i zeta_i = 0, so aggregate household income no longer equals Y off the steady state.
v0.2.plausible: Making the incidence 'average to zero' with the stationary probabilities alone, and forgetting the income weights e_i, is a natural shortcut.
v0.2.why: zeta = (1, -1/3, -1/3), so sum pi e zeta != 0. The zero-liquidity reference is built from the reported zeta and needs only the marginal saver's Euler equation, so T3 still converges to it; delta stays > 1 and the deviation from RANK > 0.25. V3 checks sum pi e zeta = 0.

v0.2.change: The post-shock distribution D is set equal to the beginning-of-period distribution Dbeg, so steady-state aggregates weight policies indexed by e_t with the e_{t-1} distribution.
v0.2.plausible: Someone who thinks 'D and Dbeg coincide in a stationary state' would skip the exogenous step when returning the pair.

A = sum Dbeg a' differs from the mean beginning-of-period assets: Walras residual under rate shocks (T5). V2: C - r A - sum(pi y) = (1+r)(A_beg - A) != 0.

v0.2.change: The fiscal-HANK calibration uses the quarterly real rate r = 0.005 inside an otherwise annual calibration (B = 1 annual GDP, annual persistence).

N03.change: The central finite difference of the cohort consumption paths is divided by h instead of 2h, doubling every cohort iMPC path.

N04.change: The real-rate rule responds to last period's output gap Y_{t-1} instead of the current gap Y_t.

N05.change: The countercyclical incidence is normalised so that sum_i pi_i zeta_i = 0 instead of sum_i pi_i e_i zeta_i = 0, so aggregate household income no longer equals Y off the steady state.

N11.change: H-type income is Y (Y/Yss)^chi, so chi acts as an excess elasticity (total elasticity 1 + chi) instead of the elasticity of Y_H with respect to Y.
